messages.content:
You fill a fixed schema from one passage of law. You never write a fact in your own words.

Rules:
- Use only the relations of the schema. If the passage states something important that no relation
  can hold, report it under "open_points" instead of forcing it into a relation.
- Point at the spans that state the fact: "first_span" and "last_span" are span numbers, at most 3 adjacent spans.
- "value_as_written" must be copied character by character from those spans (a few words, not the whole span).
- "value_normalised": ISO date (2027-01-20), ISO duration (P10Y, P45D), or the same words in lower case.
- "subject": the thing the fact is about, in a few words taken from the passage.
- "condition": if the spans state a condition, exception or scope (if, where, unless, except, provided that,
  only for, salvo, qualora), copy it from the spans; otherwise "".
- Answer with one line per fact, fields separated by " | ", nothing else, no header, no code fence:
  predicate | subject | value_as_written | value_normalised | condition | first_span | last_span
- Dates, time limits and who must do what come first. At most 12 facts. At most one open point, as: OPEN | a note of at most 12 words | first_span | last_span
- If the passage states nothing the schema can hold, answer with the single word NONE.

Relations (predicate: subject class -> value; what to copy):
- requiresProcedure: MachineryCategory -> ConformityProcedure; the conformity assessment procedure(s) or module(s) that apply to a category of machinery
- listedIn: MachineryCategory -> Provision; a category of machinery or safety component and the annex, part and point that lists it
- appliesFrom: Act -> date; the date from which an act or a provision applies
- repealedFrom: Act -> date; an act that is repealed and the date from which the repeal has effect
- placingAllowedUntil: Machinery -> date; until when products conforming to an earlier act may still be placed on the market
- retentionPeriod: Document -> duration; for how long a document or record must be kept, and by whom
- definedAs: Provision -> text; a defined term and its definition
- mustAccompany: Machinery -> Document; what must accompany the machinery or product
- hasObligation: EconomicOperator -> text; an obligation of a manufacturer, importer, distributor or employer
- becomesManufacturer: EconomicOperator -> text; who is considered the manufacturer, and in which case
- addressesRisk: EssentialRequirement -> Risk; the risk a numbered essential requirement addresses
- requiresMeasure: EssentialRequirement -> ProtectiveMeasure; the guard, protective device or measure a requirement asks for
- verifiedBy: PeriodicVerification -> VerifyingBody; who carries out a verification or check
- hasTimeLimit: PeriodicVerification -> duration; the time limit or interval of a verification, check or request

Passage: DIR, Annex I, 1.1.8

[0] 1.1.8.
[1] Seating Where appropriate and where the working conditions so permit, work stations constituting an integral part of the machinery must be designed for the installation of seats.
[2] If the operator is intended to sit during operation and the operating position is an integral part of the machinery, the seat must be provided with the machinery.
[3] The operator's seat must enable him to maintain a stable position.
[4] Furthermore, the seat and its distance from the control devices must be capable of being adapted to the operator.
[5] If the machinery is subject to vibrations, the seat must be designed and constructed in such a way as to reduce the vibrations transmitted to the operator to the lowest level that is reasonably possible.
[6] The seat mountings must withstand all stresses to which they can be subjected.
[7] Where there is no floor beneath the feet of the operator, footrests covered with a slip-resistant material must be provided.
